title: Turkey and Ham Pie
subtitle: A creamy double-crust pie for leftover roast turkey and cooked ham
excerpt: Leftover roast turkey and cooked ham in a thick cream sauce, sealed under a puff pastry lid. The ideal pie to make the day after Christmas, when the fridge has both and a deep pan of something warming is needed.
sourceNotes: A British post-Christmas staple; this version uses a puff pastry lid over a pie dish rather than a full double crust, for ease.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before the final bake. Glaze and bake from frozen at 180C for 50 to 55 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie, cover, and keep in the fridge for up to two days before baking.

content.text: This is the pie to make when you have leftover roast turkey and a piece of cooked ham in the fridge. The sauce is straightforward: butter, flour, stock, and cream, seasoned with mustard. The key is not overcooking the turkey in the sauce, since it is already cooked and will dry out if it gets too much heat.

items.prepNote: or leftover roast turkey, shredded into chunks

content.text: Melt the butter in the medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the leek and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the stock, stirring constantly. Add the cream and mustard. Stir until the sauce is smooth and thick. Add the thyme leaves and season with salt and black pepper.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Fold in the turkey, ham, and parsley. Leave to cool for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 210C. Tip the filling into a deep 23cm pie dish. The filling should sit just below the rim.

Unroll the puff pastry and lay it over the dish. Press it firmly onto the rim and trim away the excess. Brush all over with beaten egg. Score the surface lightly with a knife and cut a small slit in the centre.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden. If the pastry colours before 25 minutes, reduce to 190C for the remainder.
Rest for 10 minutes. Serve from the dish, making sure each portion gets some of the pastry lid.

items.symptom: The puff pastry doesn't rise properly.
items.cause: The filling was hot when the pastry went on, or the oven was opened during the first 20 minutes.
items.fix: Let the filling cool for at least 15 minutes. Do not open the oven door for the first 20 minutes of baking.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin after baking.
items.cause: The sauce was not thick enough before the turkey and ham went in.
items.fix: The sauce should coat the back of a spoon thickly before the meat is added. If it seems thin, simmer it for 2 more minutes before folding in the filling.

items.symptom: The pastry lid slides off when serving.
items.cause: The pastry was not pressed firmly onto the rim.
items.fix: Press the puff pastry firmly onto the dry rim of the dish. Dampen the rim with a little water before laying the pastry for better adhesion.
